name: Mailing and air-carriage restrictions by item category
description: What item categories may be mailed, and what may be carried by air, with the conditions that apply. The spine is the USPS domestic mailability list (Publication 52, Appendix A) — about 90% of records. Alongside it: UK postal (Royal Mail, Post Office, Parcelforce, Royal Mail Wholesale), the UPU prohibited-articles entries for the US and UK, and about 116 records that are not about mail at all but about US air transport — passenger baggage and air cargo under FAA PackSafe, TSA, IATA and ICAO packing instructions, and 49 CFR. All three private couriers are covered as of 2026-09-01: FedEx (the International Connect prohibited and restricted item lists), UPS (the US Tariff/Terms and Conditions of Service — the items not accepted for transportation, plus the commodity sections on alcohol, marijuana and hemp, biological substances, firearms and ammunition, dry ice, limited quantity packages, hazardous waste and mercury, live animals, perishables, portable electronic devices, and tobacco and vaping), and DHL Express US (the prohibited commodities and the items needing prior approval, from DHL's own US 'what can I ship' page). Answers 'can I mail a lighter', 'USPS lithium battery mailing rules', 'can I fly with a power bank' and 'is [item] prohibited or restricted by [carrier]'. The carrier and scope fields on each record say which question it answers: a rule about carry-on baggage is not a rule about mail.
licence: Facts extracted from public government and postal service web pages; not a reproduction of the original text

records.conditions: Should be carried in carry-on baggage; in checked baggage they must be completely powered off and protected to prevent unintentional activation or damage.
records.source_quote: When portable electronic devices powered by lithium batteries are in checked baggage, they must be completely powered off and protected to prevent unintentional activation or damage.

records.conditions: POCs do not actually contain or generate oxygen; they concentrate it from the ambient air.

records.item_category: Portable recreational vehicles powered by lithium ion batteries (hoverboards, self-balancing scooters)
records.conditions: Airline approval required for any lithium ion battery exceeding 100 Wh; a device with a battery exceeding 160 Wh is prohibited as carry-on or checked baggage.
records.source_quote: Airline approval is required for any lithium ion battery exceeding 100 watt hours (Wh).* The airline may choose to not accept the devices at all or may limit them to carry-on baggage. A device with a lithium ion battery that exceeds 160 watt hours (Wh) is prohibited as carry-on or checked baggage.

records.item_category: Power tools with rechargeable lithium batteries
records.conditions: Remove the battery and pack it in carry-on while checking the tool; checked devices must be completely powered off and protected from accidental activation within watt-hour limits.
records.source_quote: Lithium battery-powered devices like power tools can be checked only if they are completely powered off and protected from accidental activation (like in the manufacturer’s hard case) while still meeting the watt-hour (Wh) restrictions.

records.item_category: Regulated dangerous goods not otherwise listed on the PackSafe chart
records.conditions: Passengers are not allowed to carry-on or check regulated dangerous goods on passenger aircraft; if not regulated, they are allowed.
records.source_quote: Passengers are not allowed to carry-on or check regulated dangerous goods on passenger aircraft.

records.scope: checked baggage only; not allowed in carry-on
records.conditions: One self defense spray, not exceeding 118 ml (4 fluid ounces), per passenger in checked baggage only.
records.source_quote: One self defense spray, not exceeding 118 ml (4 fluid ounces), per passenger in checked baggage only.

records.item_category: Self-inflating personal safety devices (life jackets, safety vests)
records.conditions: No more than two devices, fitted with no more than two small gas cartridges per device (Division 2.2 gas only), plus no more than two spare cartridges per device.
records.source_quote: No more than two self-inflating personal safety devices, fitted with no more than two small gas cartridges per device (containing no hazardous material other than a Division 2.2 gas) for inflation purposes plus no more than two spare cartridges per device.

records.conditions: Flares and other similar flammable/explosive products are forbidden.

records.item_category: Small compressed gas cylinders and cartridges in or with a device (CO2)
records.scope: checked baggage only; not allowed in carry-on
records.conditions: Up to four cartridges/cylinders of nonflammable gas; each must not exceed 50 ml (equivalent to a 28 g CO2 cartridge); larger cylinders are forbidden unless covered by another exception.
records.source_quote: Up to four cartridges/cylinders containing nonflammable gas may be carried. Each cylinder must not exceed 50 ml (equivalent to 28 g carbon dioxide cartridge).

records.item_category: Small compressed gas cylinders for mechanical limbs

records.source_quote: Cylinders/cartridges containing nonflammable, nontoxic gases may be worn in mechanical limbs and spare cylinders/cartridges may be carried in carry-on or checked baggage.

records.conditions: With airline approval only; limited to two spare larger lithium ion batteries exceeding 101–160 Wh.

records.item_category: Batteries packed with other dangerous goods (UN 3090, UN 3480, UN 3551)
records.conditions: Must not be packed with Class 1 explosives (other than Division 1.4S), Division 2.1 flammable gases, Class 3 flammable liquids, Division 4.1 flammable solids, or Division 5.1 oxidizers.
records.source_quote: must not be packed in the same outer packaging or overpack with dangerous goods classified as: − Class 1 (explosives) other than Division 1.4S, − Division 2.1 (flammable gases), − Class 3 (flammable liquids), − Division 4.1 (flammable solids) or − Division 5.1 (oxidizers).

records.item_category: Data loggers and cargo tracking devices with installed lithium batteries
records.scope: attached to or placed in packages, overpacks or unit load devices
records.conditions: Not subject to the Regulations when in use during transport, lithium-ion not exceeding 20 Wh, lithium metal content not exceeding 1 g, and the devices cannot generate a dangerous evolution of heat.
records.source_quote: Data loggers and cargo tracking devices with installed lithium batteries, attached to or placed in packages, overpacks or unit load devices are not subject to any provisions of these Regulations provided the following conditions are met:

records.item_category: Defective, damaged or recalled lithium or sodium ion batteries
records.conditions: Batteries identified by the manufacturer as defective for safety reasons, or damaged with potential to produce a dangerous evolution of heat, fire or short circuit, are forbidden for air transport; applies also to recalled devices (Special Provision A154).
records.source_quote: Lithium or sodium ion batteries, identified by the manufacturer as being defective for safety reasons, or that have been damaged, that have the potential of producing a dangerous evolution of heat, fire or short circuit are forbidden for transport by air (e.g. those being returned to the manufacturer for safety reasons).

records.conditions: Vehicles powered by both flammable gas/liquid and a battery are classified primarily under the provisions for flammable gas or flammable liquid powered vehicles; the descriptive text 'hybrid' has been added to UN 3166 shipping names.
records.source_quote: Vehicles which are powered by both flammable gas/liquid and a battery, are classified primarily under the provisions for flammable gas or flammable liquid powered vehicles.

records.item_category: Lithium ion and sodium ion batteries — state of charge limit (UN 3480, UN 3551)
records.conditions: Must be shipped at a state of charge not exceeding 30% of rated capacity; above 30% only with the approval of the State of Origin and State of the Operator under Special Provision A331.
records.source_quote: All lithium ion cells and batteries (UN 3480) and sodium ion cells and batteries (UN 3551) must be shipped at a state of charge (SoC) not exceeding 30% of their rated capacity. Cells and/or batteries at a SoC of greater than 30% may only be shipped with the approval of the State of Origin and the State of the Operator under the written conditions established by those authorities, see Special Provision A331.

records.item_category: Lithium-ion batteries packed with equipment, UN 3481, cells/batteries over 2.7 Wh — state of charge
records.conditions: Starting January 1, 2026, must be offered for transport at a state of charge not exceeding 30% of rated design capacity where the cells or batteries have a Watt-hour rating greater than 2.7 Wh.
records.source_quote: UN 3481, lithium ion batteries packed with equipment where the cells/batteries have a Watt-hour rating greater than 2.7 Wh.

records.item_category: Lithium-ion battery powered vehicles, UN 3556, battery over 100 Wh — state of charge
records.conditions: Starting January 1, 2026, must be offered for transport at a state of charge not exceeding 30% of rated design capacity or an indicated battery capacity not exceeding 25%, where the battery exceeds 100 Wh.
records.source_quote: UN 3556, Vehicle, lithium ion battery powered where the battery has a Watt-hour rating greater than 100 Wh.

records.item_category: Lithium ion cells and batteries packed alone (UN3480) — Section II removal
records.conditions: The 63rd Edition of the IATA DGR removed Section II from packing instructions 965 and 968 for lithium cells and batteries packed alone; compliance with the revision is mandatory after March 31, 2022.
records.source_quote: Compliance with this revision is mandatory after March 31, 2022. Until that date the Section II provisions of PI 965 and PI 968 may be used as they are found in the 62nd Edition (2021) of the IATA Dangerous Goods Regulations.

records.item_category: Lithium-ion cells and batteries shipped by themselves (UN 3480)
records.conditions: Forbidden as cargo on passenger aircraft; all packages under Packing Instruction 965 Section IA and IB must bear a Cargo Aircraft Only label.
records.source_quote: All lithium-ion cells and batteries shipped by themselves (UN 3480) are forbidden for transport as cargo on passenger aircraft. All packages prepared in accordance with Packing Instruction 965, Section IA and IB, must bear a Cargo Aircraft Only label, in addition to other required marks and/or labels.

records.item_category: Lithium metal batteries packed by themselves (Packing Instruction 968) — passenger aircraft
records.conditions: Forbidden as cargo on passenger aircraft; under Special Provision A201 limited quantities may be shipped on passenger aircraft with approval of the States of Origin, Destination and Operator.
records.source_quote: Lithium metal batteries packed by themselves (not contained in or packed with equipment) (Packing Instruction 968) are forbidden for transport as cargo on passenger aircraft).

records.item_category: Lithium metal cells and batteries shipped by themselves (UN 3090)
records.conditions: Forbidden as cargo on passenger aircraft; all packages under Packing Instruction 968 Section IA and IB must bear a Cargo Aircraft Only label.
records.source_quote: All lithium metal cells and batteries shipped by themselves (UN 3090) are forbidden for transport as cargo on passenger aircraft. All packages prepared in accordance with Packing Instruction 968, Section IA and IB, must bear a Cargo Aircraft Only label, in addition to other required marks and/or labels.

records.item_category: Sodium ion cells and batteries shipped by themselves (UN 3551)
records.conditions: Forbidden as cargo on passenger aircraft; all packages under Packing Instruction 976 must bear a Cargo Aircraft Only label.
records.source_quote: All sodium ion cells and batteries shipped by themselves (UN 3551) are forbidden for transport as cargo on passenger aircraft. All packages prepared in accordance with Packing Instruction 976, must bear a Cargo Aircraft Only label, in addition to other required marks and/or labels.

records.item_category: Vehicles powered by batteries exceeding 100 Wh (UN 3171, UN 3556, UN 3557, UN 3558)
records.conditions: Must be offered for transport with batteries at a state of charge not exceeding 30% of rated capacity, or an indicated battery capacity not exceeding 25%; above 30% only with State of Origin and State of the Operator approval.
records.source_quote: Vehicles powered by batteries with a watt-hour rating exceeding 100 Wh must be offered for transport with: ▪ the battery(ies) at a state of charge not exceeding 30% of their rated capacity; or ▪ an indicated battery capacity not exceeding 25%.

records.item_category: Lithium-ion (PI 965) cells or batteries packed alone — Section IA
records.conditions: Highest restriction tier. Applies to lithium ion cells/batteries packed alone that exceed the Section IB quantity/watt-hour thresholds. Full IATA DGR compliance required including UN specification packaging, all labelling, documentation, and biennial training. No exceptions.
records.source_quote: Section IA remains unchanged.

records.item_category: Lithium-ion (PI 965) cells or batteries packed alone — Section IB
records.conditions: Applies to lithium ion cells/batteries at or below threshold watt-hour content and within the quantity limit in Table 965-IB. Full IATA DGR compliance required (including initial and biennial training) EXCEPT that UN specification packaging is not required. Effective March 31, 2022 — Section II was removed.
records.source_quote: Section IB now applies solely to lithium cells or batteries with a lithium content at or below the threshold amount and in a quantity that does not exceed that allowed in Section IB, Table 965-IB or Section IB, Table 968-IB, respectively.

records.item_category: Lithium metal (PI 968) cells or batteries packed alone — Section IB
records.conditions: Applies to lithium metal cells/batteries at or below lithium content threshold and within quantity limit in Table 968-IB. Full IATA DGR compliance required (biennial training mandatory) EXCEPT UN specification packaging not required. Effective March 31, 2022.
records.source_quote: Under the packing instructions of Section IB, a lithium ion or lithium metal cell or battery packed alone is subject to all of the applicable provisions of the IATA Dangerous Goods Regulations (including the General Requirements) except for the requirement to use a specification (UN Standard) packaging.

records.item_category: Lithium metal (PI 968) cells or batteries packed alone — Section II
records.conditions: REMOVED effective March 31, 2022. Section II previously exempted small lithium metal cells/batteries packed alone from full regulation (no training, no specification packaging). This exception no longer exists.
records.source_quote: Section II applied to: Lithium cells or batteries with a lithium content at or below the threshold amount and packed in a quantity that did not exceed that allowed in Section II, Table 965-II or Section II, Table 968-II, respectively.

records.item_category: Lithium ion batteries contained in equipment (UN 3481) — recommended 2025
records.conditions: IATA DGR recommends state of charge not exceeding 30%, or an indicated battery capacity not exceeding 25%.
records.source_quote: UN 3481, lithium ion batteries contained in equipment

records.conditions: Must be offered for transport at a state of charge not exceeding 30% of their rated design capacity.
records.source_quote: A 30% state-of-charge limit already applies to lithium batteries shipped alone by air (UN 3480).

records.item_category: Lithium ion batteries packed with equipment (UN 3481) — cells >2.7 Wh
records.conditions: Starting January 1, 2026, must be offered for transport at a state of charge not exceeding 30% of their rated design capacity.

records.source_quote: The maximum number of lithium batteries allowed in each parcel is the minimum number required to power the device plus two spares. For lithium ion/polymer batteries the Watt-hour rating must not exceed 20Wh per cell or 100Wh per battery. For lithium metal/alloy batteries the lithium content must not be more than 1g per cell or 2g per battery.

records.conditions: Samples must not exceed 5 litres/5kg; pack in a leak proof or sift proof inner protected by cushioning material in rigid outer packaging.

records.item_category: Financial documents (money, banker's drafts, cheques, bonds, securities)
records.scope: prohibited on Parcelforce Worldwide international services; UK services excluded from compensation
records.conditions: Financial documents exchangeable for money, goods or services cannot be sent on Parcelforce Worldwide international services; they can be sent on UK services but are excluded from compensation.
records.source_quote: any financial documents (money, banker's drafts, Cheques, dividends, binds securities etc.) which can be exchanged themselves or with any other document, for money goods or services cannot be sent on PFWW international services. They can be sent on PFWW UK services but are excluded from compensation.

records.item_category: Firearms classified as weapons of war (Section 5) and ammunition
records.scope: all Royal Mail and Parcelforce Worldwide services
records.conditions: May not be sent by any Royal Mail or Parcelforce Worldwide service under any circumstances; airguns, Section 1 and Section 2 firearms may be sent as guns for sporting use; deactivated, antique and imitation firearms are allowed.
records.source_quote: Firearms and their component parts classified as weapons of war (e.g. Section 5 firearms), ammunition of any kind and firearms prohibited under the Firearms Acts l968-l997 may not be sent by any Royal Mail or Parcelforce Worldwide service under any circumstances.

records.conditions: Must be packed to withstand a journey of up to two days and sent by a guaranteed next day service as a minimum within the UK; packages clearly labelled PERISHABLE; export of foodstuffs to certain destinations on Globalpriority and Globalvalue is prohibited.
records.source_quote: Fish, meat, vegetables and fruit may be sent through the post but they should be packed to withstand a journey of up to two days and must be sent by a guaranteed next day service as a minimum requirement within the UK.

records.conditions: Items bearing fictitious postage stamps or franking impressions, previously used postage, or bundles of postal items addressed to different people at different addresses are prohibited.
records.source_quote: Items bearing fictitious postage stamp or franking machine impression. Any item on which there is a stamp or franking machine impression which has been previously used to pre-pay any postal item.

records.scope: Royal Mail only; prohibited by Parcelforce Worldwide

records.source_quote: Human or animal ashes can only be sent using a Royal Mail service and must not exceed 50g in weight. These items are prohibited by Parcelforce Worldwide.

records.conditions: Indecent or obscene communications, prints, photographs, books or other articles, and parcels bearing grossly offensive, indecent or obscene words, marks or designs are prohibited; items discovered in transit are stopped and handed to Customs or the Police.

records.conditions: Live animals and reptiles are prohibited; permitted creatures include bees, caterpillars, cockroaches, crickets, earthworms, leeches, maggots, mealworms, silkworms, spiders and stick insects; items must be marked URGENT - LIVING CREATURES - HANDLE WITH CARE and sent 1st Class minimum.
